newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Late rally lifts Taiwan stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Late rally lifts Taiwan stocks to higher close.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Wednesday as late buying in blue-chip plastic and textile shares sparked what brokers said could be a recovery after weeks of bearish trade.
The weighted index rallied late to close 66.42 points or 1.04 percent higher at its intra-day high of 6,426.09. Before Wednesday, the index had lost over 200 points in October.
Turnover was a modest T$39.95 billion.
The index, which lost 65.05 points on Tuesday, had struggled in a narrow range for most of the session until late heavy buying in plastics and textiles helped trigger wider buying.
"It is very hard to say why investors all of the sudden decided to start buying," said Joe Chiou, a securities analyst for Taiwan Securities Investment.
"It is simply market psychology and Tuesday's big drop may have triggered some bargain hunting action."
The plastic sector rose 3.81 percent with Formosa Plastics, a key member of the giant Formosa Plastics group, soaring by the daily seven percent limit or T$4 to close at T$62.
Textiles gained 2.87 percent with Formosa Chemical Fibre, also a member of the Formosa Plastics group, finishing limit-up at T$33.40.
Brokers saw Wednesday's rise as mostly technical in nature and would not help launch the market into a sustainable bull run.
"The profit-taking pressure is still very strong, as there is really no encouraging factors to give the market a bigger upside room," Chiou said.
Also, the upcoming U.S. presidential election on November 5 likely would impose caution on trading as investors fear the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates following the vote, brokers added.
The market will be closed on Thursday because of national holiday. It will reopen on Friday.
A 6,350-6,450 range was seen for Friday.
